evidence: STRUCTURE SUPPORTS A GRADED REWARD. tests/scoring.toml is byte-for-byte the template policy: gates render=0.0, constraints=0.0; weights functional 0.6/polish 0.2/visual 0.2; floors functional=0.05. tests/tools/score.py computes reward = weighted mean of the three scored dimensions when gates pass and functional > 0.05, so it is continuous, not binary. Functional: 44 binary criteria, aggregation weighted_mean (functional/judge.toml:21), total weight 61.0 using the documented 1.0/1.5/2.0 scheme (judge.toml:23), max single-row share 2/61 = 3.3%. Polish: 5 binary rows, weighted_mean, weight 9.5. Visual: 5 likert rows (points=5, anchored 1-5), weighted_mean. The floor needs >3.05 of 61 functional weight points, about three standard rows, so only a near-dead app hits the floor. GATES ARE SIMPLE (Colderwater lesson 4): render = wrong password refused + seeded Recruiter signs in to a usable workspace; constraints = add one candidate, reload, independent Observer context sees it. Neither grades stage rules, conversations or live updates ('Permissions and workspace rules belong to scored outcomes'; 'Do not grade job opening, stage rules, conversations or live updates here'). NO SINGLE SHARED PRECONDITION: functional/prompt.md:13 'score EACH criterion independently, continue after failures ... A failed sibling verdict is not evidence against another row ... When a setup step fails, set up the same thing again on a new job'; prompt.md:31 'Never deduct one observed defect in more than one row'; T protocol falls back to Tomas's seeded conversation if hro_candidate_linked fails, so messaging rows do not hinge on linking. Criteria cover independent feature families (job/candidate intake, single moves, ordering, reject/reopen, interview places, roles x4, anonymous/401, stale 409, bulk x3, undo x3, activity x2, notes, live board, messaging x8, candidate view/privacy/link, restart). WORKED PARTIAL APPS (design-level, not measured): (a) server-backed board with all stage/role rules but no live push: functional loses hro_live_board 2, hro_msg_exchange 1.5, hro_unread_counts 2, hro_unread_scrolled_up 2, hro_seen 1.5 = 9/61, polish loses live_board+live_thread 4/9.5 -> mid-high reward, not 1 or 0. (b) basic CRUD board plus chat with no validation, no roles, no undo/bulk/stale handling: earns e.g. add_candidate, arrive_bottom, reorder, reject_reason, notes, msg_compose, thread_latest/earlier, drafts, restart -> low but nonzero functional, likert visual still contributes -> low reward. (c) static/browser-only app -> constraints gate 0 -> reward 0. Ordering a<golden, b<a, c<b is plausible. LESSON 2 (weights): one documented scheme, no steering. LESSON 11 / dimension-zeroing risks noted below. RESIDUAL RISKS (why risk=true): (1) No measured discrimination. raw-evidence-index.json scope says verbatim 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent.' The only runtime evidence is a scripted golden driver (via-solve.log: 26 groups PASS), which cannot show a spread across partial apps. REVIEW_POLICY requires separate hash-bound reward-discrimination records; none exist for this candidate. (2) Heavy conjunction compresses the low end: many core rows bundle basic success with edge refusals ('Fails if any condition stated above does not hold'), e.g. hro_job_open requires refusing places 0/51/2.5 and a Recruiter-as-manager replay, hro_move_one_stage requires skip refusals, hro_add_candidate requires the source shown. A partial app that does the basics but misses one edge gets 0 on that basic row, so weaker apps may cluster near the 0.05 floor; still graded, but unmeasured. (3) Each scored prompt re-runs the constraints-gate check ('gives every binary criterion 0' functional/prompt.md:13; polish/prompt.md:12) and states budget exhaustion yields binary 0 'NOT EXERCISED'; a single judge slip on that check or an exhausted 9000 s functional budget on the long S..D protocol zeroes functional, which via the floor zeroes the whole reward (Colderwater lessons 4/11). This is a judge-variance all-or-nothing path, not an app-quality one, and its frequency is unmeasured. No concrete counterexample shows the rubric is all-or-nothing, so this is not a Fail; but the row's claim is empirical and Pass would upgrade an unmeasured claim (SKILL.md 'Never upgrade an unmeasured claim to Pass').
suggested_fix: Before clearance, run the full configured verifier on the golden plus at least two mutated partial apps (e.g. live push disabled; role/undo/bulk rules removed) and record hash-bound reward-discrimination and ranking evidence showing distinct, ordered, non-floor rewards; consider whether the per-dimension repeat of the constraints-gate check is needed given gates already enforce it.
